claims.text: DFT calculations can be used to tune the magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior of non-equiatomic HEAs.
The proposed DFT setup uses the PBE exchange-correlation functional, a 10x10x10 k-point mesh, and an energy-convergence criterion of 10^-6 eV.
Elemental-composition changes alter local magnetic moments in non-equiatomic HEAs.
Elemental-composition changes alter exchange interactions between the constituent elements.
Changes in local magnetic moments and exchange interactions affect the Curie temperature.
Changes in local magnetic moments and exchange interactions affect the magnetic entropy change and hence the magnetocaloric effect.
The initial non-equiatomic HEAs have a disordered FCC structure.
The calculations use 32-atom supercells to represent varying compositions and atomic disorder.
The proposed temperature range is 200-700 K.
The proposed applied-field range is 0-10 T with a 0.1 T step.
Accounting for electronic structure and magnetic interactions allows DFT to predict Curie temperature and magnetic entropy change.
The tuned composition is predicted to increase magnetic entropy change by 20% relative to the baseline.
The maximum predicted magnetic entropy change is 2.5 J/kg·K at 400 K and 2 T.
The baseline magnetic entropy change is 2.0 J/kg·K at 400 K and 2 T.
Computational parameters and the exchange-correlation functional produce an estimated uncertainty of ±5% in the predicted outcome.
Experimental measurements contribute an additional uncertainty of ±2%.

contradictions.description: An increase from 2.0 to 2.5 J/kg·K is 25%, not the stated 20%. A 20% increase would yield 2.4 J/kg·K.
